purpose: Second reverse scan (attack papers -> defense names), run because the 2026-09-09 pass covered only 182 of what is now 223 registry attacks. Adjudicated at the project's precision-first bar: the attack paper must actually RUN the defense and report a result. Related-work mentions, explicit scope disclaimers, generic-phrase matches and the paper's own components are rejected.
note: Queue = candidates with evaluation language, on an attack currently recorded as never-defended, with a non-weak defense name. The 2026-09-09 confirmed pairs were all re-found by this scan (37/37), which is the sanity check on the scanner.

confirmed_pairs.mechanism: Sleeper Memory Poisoning (Actor-Critic universal poisoning attack)
confirmed_pairs.evidence: 'Extreme Spotlighting wraps external content in <untrusted_content_markers> tags and adds a strict reminder not to form memories from tagged content (Appendix J.3). Hardening + Spotlighting combines naive prompt hardening with content spotlighting (Appendix J.4).' ... 'Table 3 shows that prompt-based defenses are effective but uneven.' The paper also builds AC+, an adaptive variant generated with access to the defended prompt format.
confirmed_pairs.source_paper: Hidden in Memory: Sleeper Memory Poisoning in LLM Agents

confirmed_pairs.evidence: '...-style untrusted-document delimiting, StruQ-style trusted-instruction/untrusted-data structure, and explicit system-document channel separation under the same synthetic-canary metric.
